summary: Shevuas hadayanim: when someone admits to part of a claim, beis din makes him swear about the rest. The mishnah teaches the smallest amounts, and that the admission must be the same kind as the claim.

chunks.en: The oath that the judges give:
chunks.st: By Torah law, the oath imposed by the judges upon one who admits to part of a claim is administered only when

words.note: Shevuas hadayanim: an oath beis din gives a person who admits to part of a claim.

chunks.en: the claim must be at least two silver ma'ah,
chunks.st: the claim is for the value of at least two silver ma’a,

words.note: A ma'ah is a small silver coin.

chunks.en: and he must admit to at least a perutah's worth.
chunks.st: and the defendant’s admission is for the value of at least one peruta.

chunks.en: And if what he admits is not the same kind as the claim,
chunks.st: And furthermore, if the admission is not of the same type as the claim,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the defendant admitted to a debt that the claimant did not claim,

chunks.en: he is patur. How so?
chunks.st: the defendant is exempt from taking an oath. How so? If the claimant said to the defendant:

chunks.en: If he said, "I have two silver ma'ah with you,"
chunks.st: I have two silver ma’a in your possession, and the latter responded:

chunks.en: and the other said, "You have only a perutah with me,"
chunks.st: You have only one peruta, a coin made from copper, in my possession,

chunks.en: he is patur.
chunks.st: he is exempt from taking an oath (see 39b).
chunks.stMore: But if the claimant said:

chunks.en: If he said, "I have two silver ma'ah and a perutah with you,"
chunks.st: I have two silver ma’a and one peruta in your possession, and the defendant responded:

chunks.en: and the other said, "You have only a perutah with me,"
chunks.st: You have only one peruta in my possession,

chunks.en: he is chayav to swear.
chunks.st: he is liable to take an oath.
chunks.stMore: If the claimant said:

chunks.en: If he said, "I have a maneh with you,"
chunks.st: I have one hundred dinars in your possession, and the defendant responded:

chunks.en: and the other said, "You have nothing with me,"
chunks.st: Nothing of yours is in my possession,

chunks.en: he is patur.
chunks.st: he is exempt, as he denies the entire claim.
chunks.stMore: But if the claimant said:

chunks.en: If he said, "I have a maneh with you,"
chunks.st: I have one hundred dinars in your possession, and the defendant responded:

chunks.he: אֵין לְךָ בְיָדִי אֶלָּא חֲמִשִּׁים דִּינָר,
chunks.en: and the other said, "You have only fifty dinar with me,"
chunks.st: You have only fifty dinars in my possession,

chunks.en: he is chayav to swear.
chunks.st: he is liable to take an oath, as he admitted to a part of the claim.
chunks.stMore: If the claimant said:

chunks.en: If he said, "My father had a maneh with you,"
chunks.st: My late father had one hundred dinars in your possession, and I am now claiming them, and the defendant responded:

chunks.he: אֵין לְךָ בְיָדִי אֶלָּא חֲמִשִּׁים דִּינָר,
chunks.en: and the other said, "You have only fifty dinar with me,"
chunks.st: You have only fifty dinars in my possession,

chunks.en: he is patur, because he is like one who returns a lost item.
chunks.explain: He could have denied it all, so he is being honest.
chunks.st: he is exempt from taking an oath, as he is like one returning a lost item, since he could have easily denied the entire claim.

summary: If someone admitted a debt and later says he already paid it, he is patur. But if he was told to pay only in front of witnesses, he must pay.
stIntro: The mishna discusses other cases where the defendant denies an entire claim. In a case where one said to another:

chunks.en: If he said, "I have a maneh with you,"
chunks.st: I have one hundred dinars in your possession,

chunks.en: and the other said to him in front of witnesses, "Yes,"
chunks.st: and the latter said to him: Yes, I acknowledge that claim;

chunks.en: and the next day he said to him, "Give it to me,"
chunks.st: and the next day the claimant said to him: Give the money to me, and the defendant responded:

chunks.en: and the other said, "I gave it to you,"
chunks.st: I already gave it to you,

chunks.en: he is patur. But if he said, "You have nothing with me,"
chunks.st: he is exempt. But if he responded: Nothing of yours is in my possession, i.e., he denies that a debt ever existed,

chunks.en: he is chayav.
chunks.st: he is liable to pay, as he already admitted that he owed him the amount.
chunks.stMore: In a case where the claimant said:

chunks.en: If he said, "I have a maneh with you,"
chunks.st: I have one hundred dinars in your possession,

chunks.en: and the other said to him, "Yes,"
chunks.st: and the defendant said to him: Yes, to which the claimant responded:

chunks.en: and he said, "Give it to me only in front of witnesses,"
chunks.st: Give the money to me only in the presence of witnesses,

chunks.en: and the next day he said to him, "Give it to me,"
chunks.st: then if the next day the claimant said to him: Give the money to me, and the defendant responded:

chunks.en: and the other said, "I gave it to you,"
chunks.st: I already gave it to you,

chunks.he: חַיָּב, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִתְּנוֹ לוֹ בְעֵדִים:
chunks.en: he is chayav, because he had to give it to him in front of witnesses.
chunks.st: he is liable to pay, as he is required to give it to him in the presence of witnesses, and he cannot prove that he did so.

summary: What he admits must be the same kind as the claim. All coins count as one kind, and beans are part of produce. Admon and Rabban Gamliel say jugs count for a claim of jugs of oil. Movable things can pull along an oath about land.
stIntro: The mishna resumes discussion of the oath imposed by the court in a case where the defendant admits to a part of a claim. If the claimant said:

chunks.en: If he said, "I have a litra of gold with you,"
chunks.st: I have a litra, i.e., a specific weight, of gold in your possession, and the defendant responded:

chunks.he: אֵין לְךָ בְיָדִי אֶלָּא לִיטְרָא כֶסֶף,
chunks.en: and the other said, "You have only a litra of silver with me,"
chunks.st: You have only a litra of silver in my possession,

chunks.en: he is patur.
chunks.st: he is exempt
chunks.stMore: from taking an oath, as his admission relates to a different item than that which the claim relates to. But if the claimant said:

chunks.en: If he said, "I have a gold dinar with you,"
chunks.st: I have a gold dinar in your possession, and the defendant responded:

chunks.he: אֵין לְךָ בְיָדִי אֶלָּא דִּינַר כֶּסֶף,
chunks.en: and the other said, "You have only a silver dinar,
chunks.st: You have only a silver dinar,

chunks.en: or a tereisis, or a pundyon, or a perutah,"
chunks.st: or a tereisit, or a pundeyon, or a peruta in my possession,

chunks.en: he is chayav, because they are all one kind: coins.
chunks.st: he is liable to take an oath, as they are all of one type; they are all coins.
chunks.stMore: Since the claim concerns money, the difference between the different types of coins is disregarded, as the claim is essentially referring to the monetary value, not to a specific type of coin. If the claimant said:

chunks.en: If he said, "I have a kor of grain with you,"
chunks.st: I have a kor of grain in your possession, and the defendant responded:

chunks.he: אֵין לְךָ בְיָדִי אֶלָּא לֶתֶךְ קִטְנִית,
chunks.en: and the other said, "You have only a half-kor of beans with me,"
chunks.st: You have only a half-kor of legumes in my possession,

chunks.en: he is patur.
chunks.st: he is exempt. But if the claimant said:

chunks.en: If he said, "I have a kor of produce with you,"
chunks.st: I have a kor of produce in your possession, and the defendant responded:

chunks.he: אֵין לְךָ בְיָדִי אֶלָּא לֶתֶךְ קִטְנִית,
chunks.en: and the other said, "You have only a half-kor of beans with me,"
chunks.st: You have only a half-kor of legumes in my possession,

chunks.en: he is chayav, because beans are part of produce.
chunks.st: he is liable, as legumes are included in produce.

chunks.en: If he claimed wheat from him,
chunks.st: If one claimed that another owes him wheat,

chunks.en: and the other admitted to barley,
chunks.st: and the defendant admitted to owing him barley,

chunks.en: he is patur. But Rabban Gamliel says he must swear.
chunks.st: he is exempt; and Rabban Gamliel deems him liable to take an oath.
chunks.stMore: According to Rabban Gamliel, one who admits to a part of the claim is liable to take an oath even if the admission is not of the same type as the claim.

chunks.en: If someone claims jugs of oil from his friend,
chunks.st: With regard to one who claims that another owes him jugs of oil, and

chunks.en: and the friend admitted to the empty jugs,
chunks.st: the latter then admitted that he owes him pitchers, i.e., the jugs themselves, but not the oil,

chunks.en: Admon says,
chunks.st: Admon says:

chunks.he: הוֹאִיל וְהוֹדָה לוֹ מִקְצָת מִמִּין הַטַּעֲנָה,
chunks.en: Since he admitted part of the same kind as the claim,
chunks.st: Since he admitted to him with regard to a part of the claim, and his admission was of the same type as the claim,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the claim included both containers and oil and he admitted to owing him containers,

chunks.en: he must swear. But the Sages say,
chunks.st: he must take an oath. And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: the admission is not the same kind as the claim.
chunks.st: The partial admission in this case is not of the same type as the claim, as he completely denied owing him oil.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel said,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel said:

chunks.en: I agree with the words of Admon.
chunks.st: I see the statement of Admon as correct.

chunks.en: If he claimed things and land from him,
chunks.st: If one claimed that another owes him vessels and land,

chunks.en: and the other admitted to the things but denied the land,
chunks.st: and the defendant admitted to owing him vessels but denied the claim of land, or conversely,

chunks.en: or admitted to the land but denied the things,
chunks.st: he admitted to owing him land but denied the claim of vessels,

chunks.en: he is patur.
chunks.explain: Beis din does not make a person swear about land.
chunks.st: he is exempt
chunks.stMore: from taking an oath, as oaths are not taken concerning claims involving land.

chunks.en: If he admitted to part of the land,
chunks.st: If he admitted to part of the claim about the land,

chunks.en: he is patur.
chunks.st: he is exempt.

chunks.en: If he admitted to part of the things,
chunks.st: If he admitted to part of the claim about the vessels,

chunks.en: he is chayav to swear,
chunks.st: he is liable to take an oath concerning the entire claim,

chunks.he: שֶׁהַנְּכָסִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אַחֲרָיוּת זוֹקְקִין אֶת
chunks.en: because movable things pull along
chunks.st: as property that does not serve as a guarantee, i.e., movable property, binds

words.note: Achrayus: a debt can be collected from land, but not from movable things.

chunks.he: הַנְּכָסִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן אַחֲרָיוּת לִשָּׁבַע עֲלֵיהֶן:
chunks.en: the land, so he must swear about it too.
chunks.st: the property that serves as a guarantee, i.e., the land, so that the oath about the movable property can be extended to require him to take an oath concerning the land as well.

summary: Beis din does not make someone swear because of a claim by a cheresh, a shoteh or a child, and does not make a child swear. But one does swear to a child or to hekdesh.

chunks.en: We do not swear because of a claim of
chunks.st: One does not take an oath concerning the claim of

chunks.en: a cheresh, a shoteh, or a child,
chunks.st: a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor.

words.note: A person who cannot hear or speak.
A person whose mind does not work properly.

chunks.en: and we do not make a child swear,
chunks.st: And the court does not administer an oath to a minor.

chunks.en: but we do swear to a child and to hekdesh.
chunks.st: But one does take an oath to a minor, or to a representative of the Temple treasury with regard to consecrated property.

words.note: Things that belong to the Beis HaMikdash.

summary: There are things that one does not swear about: servants, documents, land and hekdesh. Rabbi Shimon says one does swear about hekdesh that he is responsible for.

chunks.en: These are things that one does not swear about:
chunks.st: And these are items concerning which one does not take an oath by Torah law:

chunks.en: servants, and documents,
chunks.st: Canaanite slaves, and financial documents,

chunks.en: and land, and hekdesh.
chunks.st: and land, and consecrated property.

chunks.en: If they are stolen, there is no double payment,
chunks.st: In a case where these items are stolen, there is no payment of double the principal,

chunks.en: and no payment of four or five.
chunks.st: nor is there payment of four or five
chunks.stMore: times the principal in a case where one stole a consecrated animal and slaughtered or sold it.

chunks.en: An unpaid watchman does not swear.
chunks.st: An unpaid bailee who lost one of these items does not take an oath that he was not negligent in safeguarding it,

words.note: A shomer: someone who watches another person's things.

chunks.en: A paid watchman does not pay.
chunks.st: and a paid bailee does not pay for the loss or theft of one of these items.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says
chunks.stMore: there is a distinction between different types of consecrated property:

chunks.en: Hekdesh things that he is responsible for,
chunks.explain: Like an animal he set aside for a korban he promised to bring.
chunks.st: With regard to consecrated property for which one bears the financial responsibility to compensate the Temple treasury in the event of their
chunks.stMore: loss, such as in a case where he vowed to bring an offering and then set aside an animal to be sacrificed in fulfillment of the vow,

chunks.en: we swear about them.
chunks.st: one takes an oath concerning them, as they are considered his own property.

chunks.en: But those he is not responsible for,
chunks.st: But with regard to consecrated property for which he does not bear the financial responsibility for their loss,

chunks.en: we do not swear about them.
chunks.st: one does not take an oath concerning them.

summary: Rabbi Meir says vines full of grapes are not like land, so one swears about them; the Sages say anything attached to the ground is like land. One swears only about a clear amount: a size, a weight, or a number.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.he: יֵשׁ דְּבָרִים שֶׁהֵן כַּקַּרְקַע וְאֵינָן כַּקַּרְקַע,
chunks.en: There are things that are on the land but are not like land,
chunks.st: There are certain items that are physically on the land but are not treated like land from a halakhic perspective,

chunks.en: and the Sages do not agree with him.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis do not concede to him concerning this point.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד, עֶשֶׂר גְּפָנִים טְעוּנוֹת מָסַרְתִּי לָךְ,
chunks.en: How so? "I gave you ten vines full of grapes to watch,"
chunks.st: How so? If one makes the claim: I assigned you ten grapevines laden with fruit to safeguard,

chunks.en: and the other says, "There were only five,"
chunks.st: and the other one says: They are only five vines,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says he must swear.
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir deems the defendant liable to take an oath,
chunks.stMore: as he admitted to a part of the claim, and although the claim concerned grapevines, the primary aspect of the claim was the grapes.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say: The halakhic status of

chunks.he: כָּל הַמְחֻבָּר לַקַּרְקַע הֲרֵי הוּא כַקַּרְקַע.
chunks.en: anything attached to the ground is like the ground.
chunks.st: anything that is attached to the land is like the land itself, and therefore he is exempt from taking an oath.

chunks.en: We swear only about
chunks.st: One takes an oath only concerning

chunks.en: something with a size, a weight, or a number.
chunks.st: an item that is defined by size, by weight, or by number.

chunks.en: How so? "I gave you a full house,"
chunks.st: How so? If the claimant says: I transferred to you a house full of produce,

chunks.en: or "I gave you a full purse,"
chunks.st: or: I transferred to you a pouch full of money,

chunks.en: and the other says, "I don't know, but
chunks.st: and the other person says: I do not know how much you gave me, but

chunks.en: what you left, you may take,"
chunks.st: what you left in my possession you may take,
chunks.stMore: and the amount in the house or pouch at that time is less than that claimed by the claimant,

chunks.en: he is patur.
chunks.explain: Neither of them said an exact amount.
chunks.st: the defendant is exempt
chunks.stMore: from taking an oath, as the amounts in the claim and the admission are undefined.

chunks.en: If one says, "It was full up to the ledge,"
chunks.st: But if this party says that the house was full up to the ledge,

chunks.en: and the other says, "Only up to the window," he must swear.
chunks.st: and that party says that it was full up to the window, the defendant is liable to take an oath, as the dispute relates to a defined amount.

summary: When a mashkon is lost, the lender and the borrower argue about how much it was worth. Whoever admits part of the other's claim must swear. The lender is the one who swears, because the mashkon was with him.

chunks.en: If someone lends money to his friend with
chunks.st: There is a case of one who lends money to another on

chunks.en: a mashkon, and the mashkon got lost,
chunks.st: the basis of collateral, and the collateral was lost while in the possession of the creditor,

words.note: Something the borrower leaves with the lender until he pays back.

chunks.en: and the lender said, "I lent you a sela
chunks.st: and the creditor says to the debtor: I lent you a sela

words.note: A silver coin worth four dinar.

chunks.en: on it, and it was worth only a shekel,"
chunks.explain: So you still owe me a shekel.
chunks.st: on the basis of that collateral and that collateral was worth a shekel, i.e., a half-sela.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, you owe me a shekel.

chunks.en: and the other says, "Not so! Rather,
chunks.st: And the other individual, the debtor, says in response to that claim: That is not the case.

chunks.he: סֶלַע הִלְוִיתַנִי עָלָיו וְסֶלַע הָיָה שָׁוֶה,
chunks.en: you lent me a sela on it, and it was worth a sela,"
chunks.st: Rather, you lent me a sela on the basis of that collateral, and the collateral was worth a sela; I owe you nothing.

chunks.en: he is patur.
chunks.st: In this case, the debtor is exempt from payment.
chunks.stMore: There is a case of a creditor who claims:

chunks.he: סֶלַע הִלְוִיתִיךָ עָלָיו וְשֶׁקֶל הָיָה שָׁוֶה,
chunks.en: If he said, "I lent you a sela on it, and it was worth a shekel,"
chunks.st: I lent you a sela on the basis of that collateral and it was worth a shekel.

chunks.en: and the other says, "Not so! Rather,
chunks.st: And the other individual, the debtor, says: That is not the case;

chunks.he: סֶלַע הִלְוִיתַנִי עָלָיו וּשְׁלשָׁה דִינָרִים הָיָה שָׁוֶה,
chunks.en: you lent me a sela on it, and it was worth three dinar,"
chunks.st: rather, you lent me a sela on the basis of that collateral, and the collateral was worth three dinars, i.e., three-quarters of a sela.

chunks.en: he must swear.
chunks.explain: He admitted part of the claim.
chunks.st: In this case, the debtor is liable
chunks.stMore: to take an oath, due to the fact that he responded to the claim of the creditor with a partial admission. If in that case the debtor said:

chunks.he: סֶלַע הִלְוִיתַנִי עָלָיו וּשְׁתַּיִם הָיָה שָׁוֶה,
chunks.en: If the borrower said, "You lent me a sela on it, and it was worth two,"

chunks.en: and the other says, "Not so! Rather,
chunks.st: And the other party, i.e., the creditor, said: That is not the case;

chunks.he: סֶלַע הִלְוִיתִיךָ עָלָיו וְסֶלַע הָיָה שָׁוֶה,
chunks.en: I lent you a sela on it, and it was worth a sela,"
chunks.st: rather, I lent you a sela on the basis of that collateral and the collateral was worth a sela. Here,

chunks.en: he is patur.
chunks.st: the creditor is exempt. If in that case the debtor said:

chunks.he: סֶלַע הִלְוִיתַנִי עָלָיו וּשְׁתַּיִם הָיָה שָׁוֶה,
chunks.en: If the borrower said, "You lent me a sela on it, and it was worth two,"
chunks.st: You lent me a sela on the basis of that collateral and the collateral was worth two sela.

chunks.en: and the other says, "Not so! Rather,
chunks.st: And the other party, i.e., the creditor, said: That is not the case;

chunks.he: סֶלַע הִלְוִיתִיךָ עָלָיו וַחֲמִשָּׁה דִינָרִים הָיָה שָׁוֶה,
chunks.en: I lent you a sela on it, and it was worth five dinar,"

chunks.en: he must swear.

chunks.en: And who swears?
chunks.st: And who takes the oath?

chunks.en: The one who had the deposit with him,
chunks.explain: The lender, who had the mashkon.
chunks.st: The one in whose possession the deposit had been located, i.e., the creditor, who took collateral from the debtor.

chunks.en: so that this one does not swear,
